title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Oakridge Capital
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrades, adding EU region, and options for a 12- vs 24-month extension with committed Dedicated capacity. Customer has concerns around data residency, KMS integration, and burst capacity costs. Agreed next steps: send updated pricing for 2-year committed Dedicated, architecture note for EU region onboarding, and schedule benchmark run (p50/p95 latency) w/ Maya and Samir next week.
topics: Renewal timing / contract length; capacity upgrade (2x GPUs) and burst; adding EU region for residency; KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence; migration plan and cutover windows; demo/benchmark scheduling; pricing and discount for 24-month commit
next_steps: Ben to send 12/24 month pricing + T&Cs by 2026-05-18
Maya to share EU onboarding + network diagram by 2026-05-20
Samir/Maya to run benchmark with p50/p95 targets next Wed 10:00 PT
Liam to schedule contract review with legal and provide timeline
action_items: Maya Singh - EU region onboarding doc + network diagram - due 2026-05-20
Ben Carter - Pricing sheet for 12m vs 24m committed Dedicated and burst costs - due 2026-05-18
Samir Patel - Provide current traffic profile and peak QPS numbers - due 2026-05-17
Liam O'Neil - Set up contract/legal review call - due 2026-05-19
transcript:
[00:00] Ben Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. i'm Ben from Redwood, i'm the AE on your account. Maya and Liam here as well. how's it going?
[00:12] Alex Rivera: good thanks, alex here. we wanted to focus on renewal items and the EU region add, have some budget questions.
[00:20] Priya Desai: yes — infra stuff, main ask is data residency, and also we need predictable throughput for end of Q3.
[00:27] Maya Singh: got it. quick agenda: pricing options for 12 vs 24 month commit, capacity upgrade (you mentioned 2x dedicated pools), EU region onboarding (VPC peering and KMS), and a short benchmark plan. does that align?
[00:40] Jordan Lee: yep that's right. also curious about burst capacity costs — last month we saw a spike and it burned unexpectedly.
[00:48] Ben Carter: right, we saw that on the dashboard. we can cap burst or set automatic fallback to hosted model to control spend, i can show cost simulations.
[00:58] Samir Patel: the spike was mainly inference requests from our trading app around 02:00 UTC, 10k QPS for 2 minutes, that's where the costs came from.
[01:09] Maya Singh: ok that helps. for Dedicated we recommend a baseline pool sized for your 95th percentile steady QPS and a small burst pool; we also have routing policies so you can fall back to a lower-cost model variant or to hosted to save money. note: KV cache — we sometimes see it transcribed as kv cash in older docs — but just to be clear, prefix and KV cache are crucial for your use case.
[01:30] Alex Rivera: on the EU region, what's the timeline to get a Private EU deployment? we need EU data residency by July.
[01:38] Maya Singh: typical EU onboarding for Redwood Dedicated + VPC peering is 4-6 weeks, can be faster if infra is ready. we'll need peering, route tables, and KMS integration details; we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. we'll draft an architecture note.
[01:54] Priya Desai: does KMS require any specific HSM vendor? we use HashiCorp vault for keys today.
[02:01] Maya Singh: we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS) and customer-managed HSMs; HashiCorp can be used via our connector, though there are a couple of config steps. we'll include those in the doc.
[02:11] Jordan Lee: security — can you confirm SOC 2 evidence and audit logs retention, our legal team will ask.
[02:16] Liam O'Neil: yeah we have SOC 2 Type II, and we can provide audit logs export and retention options; i'll append the SOC2 report link and a brief on log retention.
[02:25] Ben Carter: just calling out an earlier thread: you mentioned wanting lower p95 latency for the trading use case. what p50/p95 numbers are you currently hitting?
[02:33] Samir Patel: p50 ~ 45ms on our internal path, p95 around 220ms for long sequences, mostly because of kv cache misses during bursts.
[02:44] Maya Singh: ok that's helpful. for long sequences we can recommend quantization profiles and kernel selection that improve p95; we'll also look at longer KV cache TTL to reduce misses. we should run a benchmark with your traces — i can orchestrate it next week.
[02:59] Alex Rivera: what's the pricing delta if we go 24 months vs 12? we have headcount constraints and want to avoid mid-year renegotiations.
[03:07] Ben Carter: with a 24-month committed Dedicated contract we can offer a deeper discount on unit token pricing and waive the initial onboarding fee for an EU region. i'll send a pricing sheet with modeled scenarios.
[03:18] Priya Desai: one concern — network egress between regions; if we add EU and keep US region, will cross-region costs apply for KV cache or state?
[03:27] Maya Singh: cross-region egress charges depend on how you route. we recommend routing EU traffic to EU-only model endpoints and enabling region-specific caching to avoid cross-region KV traffic. we'll diagram that.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: do we need to change our rollout strategy? right now we have canary to 10% then full.
[03:46] Maya Singh: no change required; Redwood supports canary rollouts per route and model version pinning, and canary traffic can be isolated to region-specific pools to test EU rollouts.
[03:58] Ben Carter: quick note on burst cost controls — you can set a hard cap, but we usually recommend a staged cap and automated fallback to a cheaper model variant to avoid hard failures.
[04:10] Samir Patel: for benchmarking, what will you need from us? traces, seq length distributions?
[04:15] Maya Singh: yes — traces, QPS histograms, sample prompts; ideally a short-lived API key we can use against a mirror workload. Samir, if you can share a sanitized trace file that would be ideal.
[04:26] Samir Patel: i can do that, i'll sanitize and send before the benchmark.
[04:30] Ben Carter: cool. next steps recap: ben pricing, maya eu doc and benchmark run, liam legal loop, samir traces. any blockers?
[04:38] Alex Rivera: sounds good. one last question: if we extend to 24 months and add capacity, can we get a trial extra slot for peak testing?
[04:45] Ben Carter: we can include a one-time paid trial slot or discount the first month of excess capacity; i'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone.
[04:55] Liam O'Neil: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and next steps.
[05:00] [call ends]

Notes on transcript: transcription has a few small errors (KV cache transcribed as kv cash in one place, some names mis-attributed as Speaker 1), pauses and filler words preserved. The call lasted ~42 minutes; timestamps above are approximate and note speakers switching between named Redwood reps and customer attendees.
notes: Referenced artifacts: pricing spreadsheet (link: /redwood/pricing/OC-1423-v2.xlsx), SOC2 and compliance pack (link: /redwood/compliance/soc2-2025.pdf), EU onboarding checklist (link: /redwood/onboarding/eu-checklist.pdf). Customer asked for benchmark run and architecture note.
